CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE RAJESH RAI K  ORAL ORDER

This petition is filed under Section 528 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, to quash the proceedings against the petitioner/accused No.2 in C.C.12214/2024, arising out of Crime No.20/2024, registered by Women Police Station, Kalaburagi City, for the offences punishable under sections 498(A), 323, 504 and 506 r/w Section 34 of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, pending on the file of I Additional Civil Judge and JMFC, Kalaburagi.

entities.text: I Additional Civil Judge and JMFC, Kalaburagi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The factual matrix of the case is that, respondent No.2 married accused No.1 i.e., Vinayaka Pokarkar i.e., son of this petitioner on 15.05.2020.

During the course of marriage, NC:
2026:KHC-K:897 HC-KAR the respondent No.2's family given 15 tolas of gold and Rs.5,00,000/- of cash and other household articles to accused No.1 as a dowry.
After the marriage, respondent No.2 started to reside in the matrimony home along with her husband- accused No.1 and this petitioner/accused No.2, who is her mother-in-law.
However, they looked after her cordially for a period of 2 years.
Thereafter, this petitioner along with accused No.1 started to harass respondent No.2 both physically and mentally by demanding an additional dowry.

On 05.01.2024 at about 01.00 p.m., accused No.1 and this petitioner demanded Rs.30,00,000/- additional dowry and when respondent No.2 questioned the same, both of them thrown her out of the matrimonial home.
As such, she started to reside at her parental home.
Later, on 28.01.2024 at about 02.00 p.m., her husband i.e., accused No.1 visited her parental house and picked up a quarrel with her, assaulted her and also foisted a life threat.

Hence, respondent No.2 lodged the complaint on 21.02.2024 before respondent No.1-Police against the petitioner and her son, which came to be registered in Crime Sunanda vs The State Of Karnataka on 3 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154889880/
2 No.20/2024 for the aforementioned offences.

sentences.text: Subsequently, respondent No.1-Police investigated the case and laid charge NC: 2026:KHC-K:897 HC-KAR sheet against the petitioner and her son for the aforementioned offences by arraying this petitioner as accused No.2.
The learned Magistrate took cognizance of the offences.
Aggrieved by the same, the petitioner/accused No.2 preferred this petition to quash the proceedings against her.

3. Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent No.1 - State and learned counsel for respondent No.2.
4.

Apart from urging several contentions, the learned counsel for the petitioner has contended that,
the petitioner being accused No.2 has no knowledge whatsoever about the alleged physical and mental harassment meted out by accused No.1 to respondent No.2.
Further, it is contended that, the allegations in the complaint and statement of witnesses are omnibus allegations.
In such circumstances, it is prayed to quash the proceedings.

5. Per contra, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has contended that, now the investigation has been completed and charge sheet has been laid by respondent No.1-Police against accused No.1 and the petitioner/accused No.2.
NC: 2026:KHC-K:897 HC-KAR
Further, the statement of CW.2 and 3 i.e., eye witnesses to the incident also categorically stated the involvement of this petitioner in the alleged offence.

Moreover,
this petitioner is residing in the shared roof along with accused No.1-her son and respondent No.2.
In such circumstances, proceedings cannot be quashed against her.
Accordingly, prays to dismiss the petition.
6. Learned HCGP also opposed to petition and prays to dismiss the same.
7. I have given my anxious consideration both on the submissions made by the learned counsel for the respective parties and also perused the materials placed before this Court.

8. As could be gathered from records, the complaint averments clearly disclose that, after the marriage of respondent No.2 with accused No.1, she resided with accused Nos.1 and 2 i.e., her husband and mother-in-law respectively, for a period of 2 years and both her husband and this petitioner/accused No.2 started to harass her to bring additional dowry.

It is specifically stated in the complaint that, on 05.01.2024, both accused No.1 and this petitioner NC: 2026:KHC-K:897 HC-KAR demanded Rs.30,00,000/- from respondent No.2 as additional dowry to clear their debts.
Further, on perusal of the statements of CW.2 and CW.3 i.e., eyewitnesses to the incident, they have categorically stated the act of the accused No.1 and this petitioner/accused No.2.

In such circumstances, as rightly contented by the learned counsel for respondent No.2, the petitioner is sharing the common roof with accused No.1, at this stage, the proceedings cannot be quashed against the petitioner/accused No.2, since there are prima facie allegations and materials are forthcoming against her.
9. Hence, the petition lacks merits and the same is dismissed.
